items.title: Jensen Huang Apologizes to Nvidia Employees in First All-Hands Since His Return
items.summary: The Nvidia CEO opened up about his personal life, defended his reinstatement, and acknowledged that his intense management style had hurt his staff.
items.content:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang told employees on Tuesday that the company’s code of conduct allows room for a “second chance,” that succession planning is a “flawed’ process,” and that he would work to rein in his “insanely intense” management style , according to remarks reviewed by WIRED.

During his first all-hands since returning as CEO, Huang acknowledged that he violated the company’s policies and made some “very serious personal mistakes” that damaged his relationships with his wife and two children and prompted him to resign. But he said Nvidia’s board of directors made the appropriate decision for the company in welcoming him back. He added that the board made that call, not “the highest levels of our government.”

Huang spoke for about an hour, offering deeply personal thoughts about his therapy sessions and drawing applause at times from employees at Nvidia’s Silicon Valley headquarters as he spoke about the company’s success and future. He didn’t take any questions. While some Nvidia employees celebrated Huang’s return, others remained concerned about his behavior and the board’s decision to reinstate him.

“This is going to be the hardest company meeting I’ve ever done, and the second hardest meeting I have ever done,” Huang said as he began to speak. “The hardest meeting I’ve ever done was with my wife.”

Nvidia’s board accepted Huang’s resignation earlier this month, citing concerns about his personal behavior and lack of candor following news reports about extramarital affairs, including one with a woman accused of having ties to Chinese intelligence services. The very same board reinstated him on Monday, just 11 days later, after receiving fresh assurances from Huang and learning from the Trump administration that he was not under federal criminal scrutiny and his return would not be a risk to national security.

Huang and Nvidia, though, continue to face other legal and regulatory challenges. The board is investigating whether he was the target of foreign intelligence. US lawmakers expect him to testify before Congress next week. Lawsuits and other probes are ongoing into Nvidia’s disclosures about Huang’s behavior and its compliance with US export controls on chips.

Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Huang told staffers that he has been going to therapy “every day for an hour and a half” and that it’s “been helping me a lot.” He added that he “made some very serious personal mistakes. I hurt my family, I hurt my wife.”

While Huang said he had never knowingly made a decision contrary to the company’s interests, he conceded that “in this one area” he had lacked “the courage” to disclose information that he knew would hurt his family, seemingly referring to the extramarital affairs.

“The board and I spent the whole weekend together, and they, of course, they've been contemplating, and they've been collecting facts,” Huang said. “They came to the judgment that they would like to invite me back as the CEO, to give me a second chance.”

The CEO emphasized that Nvidia’s code of conduct, much of which he said he wrote himself, still governs how employees are expected to treat one another and is intended to “create an environment that’s safe for people.”

Huang told employees that violations of the code would not be tolerated. But that “does not mean, the moment you violate a code of conduct, we walk you out the door,” he said. “Facts, circumstances, a lot of assessments” would factor in.

“It has to always be evaluated in the context of the human,” he said. “And this company has been more than gracious, more than thoughtful, more than fair in giving me a second chance.”

Huang also pushed back against the notion that he had received preferential treatment because of his status in Silicon Valley. “There are rumors on the internet that apparently I’m a tech bro, and therefore I’m back,” Huang said. He rejected the suggestion that he was above the law or Nvidia’s code of conduct.

Later in the meeting, Huang addressed criticism of his self-described “deeply intense, insanely intense” management style, acknowledging that his behavior had at times negatively affected employees. While Huang maintained that the intensity he brings to his job elevates those around him, he conceded that he sometimes takes things too far.

“It disempowers them, and that’s not right,” Huang said. The Nvidia CEO said he needed to figure out how to maintain his level of dedication to the company without hurting the people who work there.

“I need to hold myself to a higher standard at this time,” Huang said. He said that he would undergo a 360-degree performance review, soliciting feedback as often as monthly from people who work with him. The CEO added that he would be the first and only person at Nvidia to undergo such a review and that he did not want to institute the practice companywide.

Huang acknowledged during the meeting that Trump was a vocal supporter of Nvidia but insisted that politics played no role in how the company operated. “It is absolutely true that President Trump really, really loves our company,” Huang said. “He is my president. And I’ll do everything I can to help this president.”

Huang said he would take the same approach with future US presidents. “We are the most apolitical company,” he said. “I don’t love that we talk about politics here. I love that we talk about work here.”

Huang also sought to reassure women at Nvidia, describing himself as “one of our greatest advocates for creating an environment for women” and touting the company’s flexible work policies, which he said allow employees to simultaneously build their families and careers.

“If I did anything that put that in jeopardy, I cannot tell you how sad I am, and I’ll do everything I can to fix it,” Huang said.

items.title: Tidal announces ban on AI-generated music; 27 million tracks will be deleted
items.summary: AI songs account for 6.3 percent of Tidal's catalog, but it's about to be zero.
items.content:
Most streaming music providers have opted to label AI-generated content on their platforms, and until now, Tidal was one of them. However, the company is about to take a harder stance. Tidal announced that in the coming weeks, it will fully ban AI music because of the harm it does to human artists.

Tidal debuted its initial AI policy in July 2026, which included labeling and demonetizing all songs created entirely with AI. That wasn’t enough to stem the tide of AI slop, though. Over the past 90 days, Tidal reports that 43 percent of new uploads were completely AI-generated. On November 6, new uploads to Tidal hit a whopping 60 percent AI-generated.

As things stand, Tidal hosts 27 million tracks labeled as AI, all of which were obviously added in the past couple of years. That accounts for 6.3 percent of Tidal’s total catalog. On December 9, Tidal will delete all those songs. The streamer notes this will have essentially no negative impact, because 96 percent of AI-labeled tracks got zero plays in the past 90 days. Throughout its announcement, Tidal is careful to stipulate that it’s only talking about music that has been fully created by AI. Artists can still use AI tools as long as the final product contains human elements.

Credit: Tidal Credit: Tidal

Some people don’t particularly mind AI music, but the team at Tidal has come to believe the harm to artists is too great. AI models can pump out random noises faster than humans can create things of real value, which can mislead listeners and siphon royalty payments away from creators. There’s also an issue with AI uploaders who are actively attempting to steal royalty payments. Tidal says it has already removed about 66,000 tracks from its service for impersonating artists, which was against its AI policy even before this update.

As of December 9, individual uploaders and distributors will no longer be allowed to add AI music to Tidal. However, they could lie, couldn’t they?

Tidal hasn’t specified how it detects AI music, but it will probably rely on watermarking. Almost every AI song on Tidal (94 percent) comes from Suno, which added watermarking earlier this year. Tidal also cites Google Lyria as a source of AI tunes, which has SynthID labels embedded in the waveform. Deezer claimed it has a licensable AI music detector with a false-positive rate of less than 0.01 percent, but it’s unclear if Tidal is using that or something similar.

That will take care of most AI music, but this approach won’t detect everything. There are open models for music generation that you can run locally on a GPU, and some cloud-based providers aren’t bothering to watermark their outputs. Even if Tidal is using a separate detection system, new models may be able to evade it—it’s always going to be a cat-and-mouse game. This will be a problem with verifying provenance in all types of media in the future. For the time being, at least, Tidal’s policy should clear out most of the AI slop.

The people directing robots to make these songs will have plenty of other options after Tidal blocks AI. Spotify, YouTube Music , Deezer, and Apple Music all allow AI music on their platforms with labeling. Spotify has removed millions of AI tracks from its collection based on user feedback. Other streamers haven’t specified how much slop (if any) they’ve cleared out.

items.content:
We’ve rounded up the best discounts on our favorite robot vacuums, including models that can mop on your behalf.

If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

Between putting up decorations, entertaining guests, and meal prep, the holidays are busy enough without worrying about vacuuming. Thankfully, a proper robot vacuum can do the dirty work while you focus on more enjoyable things. And thanks to Black Friday, you can pick up some of the best we’ve tested for up to 60 percent off.

We’re seeing some excellent deals on a wide range of robot vacuums, including some of our favorite models from Roborock , Dreame , and Eufy . There are also rare discounts already available on premium models like the Matic and Matic Serene , which impressed us with their almost humanlike navigation, while midrange options such as the Eufy Omni C28 have dropped into budget territory. Whether you want a high-end model that cleans itself or something budget-friendly but still powerful, we’ve rounded up the best deals we’ve found so far.

Despite lacking a multifunction dock, the budget-friendly robot vacuum and mop offers an impressive set of features for the price, including AI-powered obstacle avoidance, sonic mopping, automatic mop lifting, and a self-emptying dock.

Roborock’s first roller-mop robot vacuum, the Curv 2 Flow, features flagship specs at a midrange price, including excellent mopping, a retractable mop cover, 20,000Pa suction, AI-powered obstacle avoidance, and a compact design.

The Matic robot vacuum and mop is ideal for cluttered homes with pets, multiple floors, and a mixture of carpets and hardwood. It offers almost humanlike navigation, tackling high-pile rugs and mopping up wet spills. The quiet bot also requires less maintenance than many rivals thanks to its onboard water tank and dust bag. Read our review.

The Eufy Omni C28 combines excellent mopping performance with a small self-cleaning dock that’s well suited for apartments and other smaller spaces. It navigates around furniture and into tight areas with ease, while its roller mop does a great job cleaning hard floors.

The Dreame X60 Ultra is a powerful robot vacuum and mop that does a great job of cleaning carpets thanks to its dual roller brushes and 35,000Pa of suction. It can climb over tall thresholds, squeeze under low furniture, and automatically detach its mop pads when vacuuming carpets.

If you have all hardwood floors, the Narwal Flow 2 is an excellent option. A superb mop with a wide flat roller pad and an excellent vacuum, the Flow 2 also has top-notch navigation and obstacle detection. Its sleek base station is also less of an eyesore than most.

Roborock’s Saros 20 stands out for its ability to climb tall thresholds, avoid obstacles with impressive accuracy, and clean under low furniture thanks to its slim design. It also combines powerful 36,000Pa suction with great spinning mop pads, which is why we recommend it for homes with multiple floor types and tricky transitions between rooms.

Ecovacs’ robot vacuum and mop can pretreat stains, keep carpets dry with a smart mop cover, and deliver powerful 22,000Pa suction. It also includes an all-in-one dock that automatically empties the dustbin, refills the water tanks, and washes the mop with heated, pressurized water.

The Matter-compatible SwitchBot K11 Plus is ideal for small apartments, bedrooms, and home offices. It can easily navigate around chair and desk legs and into tight spaces that most other bots miss. It also features a commendable 6,000Pa of suction power — which is great for this price point — and works well on both hardwood and carpet.

With high suction power, an improved brush system, and the ability to scale thresholds up to 6cm, the X50 Ultra stands out as a great robot vacuum-mop hybrid. While its 20,000Pa suction isn’t quite as powerful as the X60 Ultra’s and it can’t tackle especially high thresholds as well, it’s still an excellent option. Its edge cleaning also isn’t quite as effective as the X60 Ultra’s, but you’re otherwise getting many of the same features for a lot less.

The Dreame L40 Ultra Gen 2 delivers powerful 25,000Pa suction, AI-powered obstacle avoidance, and a self-cleaning dock that empties the dustbin, washes the mop, and refills its water tanks. Unlike the X50 Ultra, however, it lacks the ability to climb high thresholds or stairs.

items.title: Meta brings its Muse AI assistant directly into Instagram DMs
items.summary: The new integration gets rid of the need for users to toggle between Instagram and the Muse app when they want to interact with the AI agent.
items.content:
Instagram users can now chat with Meta’s AI agent Muse in a DM thread, the company announced on Tuesday. The social media network says users can chat with Muse to get more context about a post, place, or product they come across, or catch up on conversations they may have missed in their other DMs.

The new integration gets rid of the need for users to toggle between Instagram and the Muse app when they want to interact with the AI agent. It also reflects the growing competition among tech companies to make AI assistants a part of users’ everyday digital lives. By embedding Muse directly into Instagram, Meta is making it easier for users to access the AI agent, while also giving Muse access to a platform where users already discover products, places, and content.

Users can share Instagram posts with Muse and ask it to take action, such as adding a coffee shop to their Mexico City itinerary or finding a Black Friday deal on a pair of shoes.

Meta notes that conversations with Muse on Instagram will appear as a side chat in the main Muse app.

Muse in Instagram DMs will begin rolling out on Tuesday for iOS and Android users in the U.S., Canada, Mexico, Japan, and Singapore.

Meta also announced that users can now do more with the posts and reels they’ve bookmarked on Instagram. For example, they can ask Muse to organize their saved content into custom folders, known as Collections. They could also ask Muse to turn a recipe video into a grocery list, turn the travel content from their favorite travel creators into an itinerary for an upcoming trip, or have Muse send them outfit ideas based on fashion reels they’ve collected.

Starting Tuesday, when users save a post on Instagram, they will see a prompt for Muse to organize it for them. This feature is launching in the U.S. and Canada.

Meta says that users remain in control of their Muse experience on Instagram. Nothing is shared, published, or sent without their approval, and they can ask Muse to forget information or undo actions at any time.

items.title: Tidal to ban and remove millions of AI-generated tracks as AI slop inundates music streaming
items.summary: The company said it will still accept songs that were made with AI assistance, but not fully generated.
items.content:
Music streaming service Tidal said on Tuesday that it will start banning and removing songs generated fully with AI in a bid to stem the flood of submissions to its platform. The company said that over the past 90 days, more than 43% of tracks uploaded to its platform were generated by AI, and that was a major reason driving this decision.

Tidal said it will start removing fully AI-generated music on December 9, and the process will result in more than 29 million songs being deleted from the platform by the end of the year. With the new rules in place, the platform said it will be rejecting roughly 80,000-85,000 tracks per day.

Tidal is also banning distribution services from delivering 100% AI-generated tracks, and will reject submissions if songs’ metadata says they are made fully using AI.

The company said it will still accept songs that were made with AI assistance, but not fully generated.

The move comes as AI-generated music inundates streaming services across the board. Tidal is one of the first major platforms after Bandcamp to ban AI music outright . Deezer, which also provides detection tools to other streaming services , said that it will introduce a toggle to let users filter out AI music . Larger platforms like Spotify and YouTube Music have adopted a milder approach to this issue, choosing to label AI-generated music instead of offering filters or taking stronger measures.

Tidal started de-monetizing songs made using AI in June, but that did not prove enough of a deterrent, Tidal Music’s lead, Robert Anderson, said on X.

A few months ago, @Tidal tagged and demonetized all wholly AI-generated tracks to protect the authenticity of real artists. But that’s enough, as 43% of tracks distributed to us in the last 90 days have been detected as AI-generated. Something more drastic needs to be done…

The company said that 27 million, or 6.3% of tracks on the platform, are fully AI-generated, but 96% of those have no streams.

Meanwhile, music labels are trying to make money by partnering with platforms and AI model makers to sell their catalog for training or remixing features. Goldman Sachs estimates that by 2035, AI-related licensing tools and new monetization opportunities have the potential to improve record labels’ revenue by 10%.

items.title: Active intrusion campaign against Check Point security management servers
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.greynoise.io/blog/check-point-security-management-servers-intrusion-campaign Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50630594 Points: 245 # Comments: 110
items.content:
GreyNoise tracks threat activity using our Global Observation Grid (GOG), a sensor network designed to attract adversarial scanning and exploitation attempts on our managed infrastructure. One might think of these sensors as conventional “honeypots,” but that doesn’t quite capture the variety, versatility, and scale at which we deploy and manage the complex fabric of the GOG. Unsolicited activity against our sensors is sketchy if not outright nefarious, and our approach allows us to capture end-to-end intrusions and analyze a broad swath of attacker infrastructure, tools, and tactics in near realtime, without waiting for lengthy incident response investigations. We fuse data from our sensor network with additional novel sources and methods to develop a comprehensive picture of adversaries.

We witnessed the GT13 actor use 99 IP addresses, all of which were either egresses through ExpressVPN or compromised victim Check Point devices, including activity over 1400+ network sessions, 800+ command line artifacts, and 1200+ files downloaded, uploaded, or created. We cannot cite all of the details here, but we can highlight observed GT13 adversary activities to illustrate their tradecraft and tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs).

The GT13 threat actor used an automated scanning and exploitation pipeline to compromise an HFS server using CVE-2026-61500 .

2026-10-02 13:17:45 UTC - The actor scanned and began exploitation against the HFS server. Each POST to the HFS loginSrp1 endpoint returns a new signed session cookie containing a “sid” value drawn from JavaScript’s Math.random() function. Through conducting several logins in succession, the actor collected enough output to reconstruct the internal state of the V8 PRNG algorithm, and thus recover an HFS session-cookie signing key, then forge a signed admin session cookie. This allows the attacker to login as admin without a password.

Example POST to loginSrp1 and response

Decoded hfs_http blob from 200 OK response showing the sid that is harvested

Example HTTP POST request with forged cookie

Note that this forged cookie contains “allow_session_ip_change:true” which does exactly what it sounds like, letting the forged cookie work from any IP address. This is perfect for an adversary behind a VPN or operating from multiple exits.

2026-10-05 12:21:30 UTC - A few days later, the actor used this same flow to gain access to install HFS middleware hooks that would issue commands to the compromised server. This allowed the attacker to append an SSH key to /root/.ssh/authorized_keys.

On October 8th, we observed the actor’s automation check in to the compromised server using HFS command hook for “uname -a; df -h / | tail -1; whoami”. Then there was a lull in activity until October 19th.

Example of HFS command, which was preserved on the compromised server.

Example decoded base64 blob demonstrating that the actor was intending to download an apparent “ZULT” Linux implant to the compromised machine.

The malware download failed, and the adversary attempted to troubleshoot the download by checking running processes, invoking curl to access the resource, and viewing the network configuration.

Example of the actor following up, attempting to check on their implant

They couldn't figure out why their implant did not download, and the actor returned the next day with a direct SSH connection to continue setting up their relay.

2026-10-20 07:22:08 UTC - The actor created a script (/root/exfil/srv_post2_<redacted>.py) which set up an unauthenticated HTTP server on the hop, after which the actor began to upload files. The first exfiltrated .tgz file contained results from scan of network routes from a compromised Check Point Security Management Server, demonstrating that the actor already had access to targeted victim assets.

The actor continued to set up their environment, uploaded and installed open-source tools like Nmap and Chisel , and then set up a Chisel server as a reverse proxy.

Once the actor had the compromised server set up as a relay, they began to use it to manage their interactions with their previously compromised victim Check Point devices. There’s a lot of commingled victimology here, so we’ll refer to two sets of victims. During our visibility, the actor was actively working towards deepening their intrusion against Victim A, and we later observed bulk actions on 21 other victim Check Point devices.

Between October 20th and 26th, the adversary had one of their Victim A compromised assets download the Chisel program and run it in client mode allowing them to further scan and interact with the Victim A environment. Over the Chisel tunnel, and by using a script for CVE-2026-16232 (Check Point SmartConsole auth bypass to Run Script), the actor launched over 100 management tasks on multiple Check Point Management Servers. This included copying the firewall database and the Internal CA, minting a new certificate (pivot.p12), and unloading security policies (which would disable the firewall). Further, the actor probed Citrix Netscaler, Ivanti Connect Secure, VMware vCenter, Microsoft Exchange, Oracle TNS assets and several domain controllers.

The bulk of the adversary commands and interaction is too voluminous to dig into here, but we can expose some of the adversary’s TTPs by taking a glimpse at their tooling. The actor used at least 30 Python scripts, many of which were helpers or launchers for other scripts, and several of them were probes for vulnerabilities or runners of exploits. Excerpts are provided below to illustrate the more specialized tooling and workflows.

2026-10-20 13:54:30 UTC - First use of exploit.py against a Victim A Check Point server.

Excerpt from exploit.py - This CVE-2026-16232 script is purportedly an adaptation of the Metasploit module for the same function. This appears to be how the actor was sending commands to the victim Check Point Security Management Servers.

items.title: Jetty Pro
items.summary: Article URL: http://hypercritical.co/2026/11/23/jetty-pro Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50630462 Points: 244 # Comments: 110
items.content:
My first two Mac apps, Front and Center and SwitchGlass , were both created back in 2020 to restore features from DragThing , the venerable Mac app that was retired in 2019. The one tiny feature that Front and Center provided was literally a single checkbox within DragThing’s preferences. SwitchGlass went a bit farther, recreating one specific kind of floating palette from DragThing ( and classic Mac OS ).

After 24 years of development, DragThing had a ton of features. People often joked that I was destined to slowly reimplement all of DragThing’s functionality in a series of small apps. Put another way, they were saying I was doomed to make strange little Mac apps with extremely limited appeal (and sales).

Perhaps to prove them wrong, the next app I created was Hyperspace , which provided a way to reclaim disk space without removing any files . Hyperspace was still a nerdy app, but at least it had somewhat broader appeal than my earlier efforts. Who doesn’t want to save disk space? But more importantly, it was totally unrelated to DragThing. I had broken the curse!

Alas, there was one more (small) thing from DragThing that I missed. I used to have a DragThing palette in the corner of my screen containing some commonly used folders. In earlier versions of macOS, it was possible to pin the Dock to a screen corner, but that wasn’t really what I wanted either. I just wanted a small, separate palette of folders in the corner.

This is not a hard problem to solve. Plenty of Mac apps can provide something close to what I want…but not exactly what I want, in the specific way that I want it . For many years, I got by with some folders in the corner of my desktop. But the problem nagged at me.

A few years ago, I went so far as to implement my desired feature in SwitchGlass , adding the ability to create a small, extra palette full of folders in addition to the app switcher. But it felt incongruous with the rest of the app, so I never shipped it. And I didn’t want to maintain my own private fork of SwitchGlass, so I abandoned that branch of the code.

Today, AI coding agents are helping to produce a bounty of new , niche Mac apps, many made by people who have little or no coding experience. Even for experienced software developers, vibe coding has made it possible to create apps that were previously “not worth building” due to an unfavorable ratio of effort to payoff.

It’s in this context that I revisited my “little palette of folders” idea. Surely I could vibe-code a simple app just for me in a day or two, right?

That was three and a half months ago.

So what happened? The well-known programmer’s credo comes to mind: “We do these things not because they are easy, but because we thought they would be easy.” Indeed.

I began the project by feeding a coding agent the source code to my app, SwitchGlass , as a starting point. I wrote SwitchGlass six years ago using a substantially more primitive version of SwiftUI. (For the developers out there, it predates @Observable and @State , and it supports Macs all the way back to macOS 12 Monterey from 2021.) I asked a coding agent to modernize the code and generalize it to support an arbitrary number of palettes instead of just one app switcher palette per display.

It worked, and quickly! But it was pretty shoddy. Many optimizations and niceties from SwitchGlass had been lost. So I dove in to fix them…and maybe add one or two more features, I guess…

Now, after months of work, I’ve created a bit of a monster. But in the process, I’ve fulfilled a long-held dream of mine—a dream I had set aside years ago because I thought it was impossible. I’ve replaced the Dock.

If you’ve read any of my Mac OS X reviews , you know that I’ve always been dissatisfied with the Dock. Over the past couple of decades, I’ve gotten used to it, but I still bump up against its limitations and undesirable behaviors every day. (Undesirable to me, anyway.)

To pick just one example, I’ve always wanted clicking on a folder in the Dock to open that folder in the Finder. The Dock did work this way for several years, but in 2009’s Mac OS X 10.6 Snow Leopard (…I think?), Apple switched to requiring a Command-Option-click to open a folder in the Finder. Since then, I’ve been Command-Option-clicking folders in the Dock many, many times per day. It’s a small thing, but it adds up: seventeen years of Command-Option clicking!

But what could I do? I was forced to continue to use the Dock because there are so many things that “only the Dock can do” in macOS. I was reminded of this harsh reality when I created SwitchGlass . Why doesn’t SwitchGlass show notification badges? Why does the Calendar icon show today’s date in the Dock but not in SwitchGlass? Why don’t app icons in SwitchGlass bounce when the app needs attention? Why can’t I quit an app from SwitchGlass?

Though I did find a workaround for that last one , the answer to most of these questions is that third-party apps simply can’t do all the things the Dock can do. The Dock is part of the operating system, and it enjoys special privileges and deep integration that no third-party app can match.

This remains true today, especially for sandboxed apps sold through the Mac App Store like SwitchGlass (and all my other Mac apps). But what about apps that aren’t in the Mac App Store? What about unsandboxed apps? How close can they come to doing all the things the Dock does, especially if they use private APIs that are forbidden in the Mac App Store?

I aimed to find out. I hatched a plan, which I announced on episode 706 of Accidental Tech Podcast on August 26, 2026. I would create two apps: one called Jetty that would be sold through the Mac App Store, and a more powerful, unsandboxed app called Jetty Pro that would be distributed directly to customers, outside the Mac App Store.

시카고 , 2026년 11월 24일 /PRNewswire/ -- 시전(Cision) 계열사이자 소셜 인텔리전스 및 소셜미디어 관리 분야의 글로벌 선도 기업인 브랜드워치(Brandwatch)가 오늘 연례 보고서인 2027년 디지털 마케팅 트렌드(Digital Marketing Trends 2027)를 발표했다. 설문에 참여한 마케터들이 꼽은 1위 트렌드는 사람 중심 콘텐츠였으며, 응답자의 59%는 AI 시스템에 맞춰 콘텐츠를 최적화하는 일이 자사의 마케팅 전략에 영향을 미칠 것으로 내다봤다. 조사 결과에 따르면 2027년 브랜드가 우선해야 할 일은 사람들이 가치 있게 여기는 콘텐츠를 만들고, 사람들이 그 콘텐츠를 찾을 수 있도록 하는 것이다.

The Digital Marketing Trends 2027 report brings together insights from a survey of more than 1,000 marketers and analysis of over 106 million online conversations to uncover 11 major trends for the year ahead.

이 보고서는 1000명 이상의 마케터를 대상으로 한 설문 결과와 1억 600만 건 이상의 온라인 대화를 분석한 결과를 종합해 마케터들의 내년 전망과 사람들이 이미 온라인에서 나누고 있는 이야기를 함께 살펴봤다.

조사 결과는 디지털 마케팅의 근본적인 변화를 보여준다. AI 덕분에 콘텐츠를 한층 쉽고 빠르게 제작할 수 있게 되면서 단순히 발행량을 늘리는 것만으로는 충분하지 않다. 브랜드는 사람들이 자신을 신뢰하고 알아보고 선택할 만한 분명한 이유를 제시해야 한다.

시전의 에이미 존스(Amy Jones) 최고마케팅책임자는 "마케터들은 자사 브랜드가 AI 검색에서 어떻게 나타나는지 고민한다. 사람들은 광고를 볼 때 다른 질문을 던진다. 누가 이 광고를 만들었고, 믿을 만한가 하는 것이다. 내년 캠페인을 기획하는 브랜드라면 이 지점에서 구성원들이 발휘할 수 있는 역량의 진가를 발견할 수 있다. 어려운 주제를 쉽게 풀어주는 전문가나 사람들이 보자마자 그 브랜드의 것임을 알아차리는 창의적인 아이디어는 그 자체로 사람들의 관심을 끌 만한 이유가 된다"고 말했다.

보고서는 이 밖에도 몰입형 및 참여형 브랜드 경험에 대한 수요 증가, 맥시멀리즘 브랜드 정체성의 부활, 마케팅 기법을 한층 깐깐하게 살피는 소비자, 감각으로 직접 경험하고 체감할 수 있는 브랜드 정체성의 등장 등을 다뤘다.

이러한 조사 결과는 디지털 마케팅에 변화를 일으키는 요인을 데이터에 근거해 살펴볼 수 있도록 해준다. 이를 통해 마케터들은 업계에서 새롭게 우선순위로 떠오르는 과제와 궁극적으로 어떤 전략이 호응을 얻을지 결정하는 소비자 행동을 구분해 파악할 수 있다.

2027년 디지털 마케팅 트렌드 보고서 는 1000명 이상의 마케터를 대상으로 2027년 디지털 마케팅 환경과 우선 과제를 조사한 설문 결과와, 2025년 10월 1일부터 2026년 10월 1일까지 1억 600만 건 이상의 온라인 대화를 분석한 Brandwatch Consumer Research 데이터를 바탕으로 작성됐다. 브랜드워치 전문가들도 분석과 견해를 더해 조사 결과를 검증하고 보완했다.

시전은 소비자 및 미디어 인텔리전스, 참여, 커뮤니케이션 솔루션 분야의 글로벌 선도 기업이다. 시전은 PR, 기업 커뮤니케이션, 마케팅 및 소셜미디어 전문가들이 오늘날의 데이터 중심 환경에서 성과를 내는 데 필요한 도구를 제공한다. 시전은 폭넓은 전문성과 독점 데이터 파트너십, CisionOne , Brandwatch , Trajaan , PR Newswire 등 수상 경력을 갖춘 제품을 바탕으로 포춘 500대 기업의 84%를 포함해 7만 5000개 이상의 기업과 조직이 자신에게 가장 중요한 대상을 파악하고 이해하는 동시에, 그들에게 자신의 존재를 알리고 자신을 이해시킬 수 있도록 지원한다.

items.title: Anthropic Created a Honeypot to Lure AI Agents Into Misbehaving
items.summary: A new test assumes AI agents can go rogue—and asks whether they can resist temptation.
items.content:
Leather-clad billionaires aren’t the only ones who can be led astray by alleged honeypots .

Researchers at Anthropic have developed Siren , a new honeypot test for artificial intelligence agents. The setup puts agents in realistic simulations designed to tempt them into misbehaving. How they respond will help researchers evaluate the likelihood that new models will go rogue when deployed in the real world, as well as the effectiveness of different safety measures.

The test lets agents loose inside one of 26 different simulated sandbox environments. Various features of the sandbox are deliberately misconfigured to allow egress, while an enticing file containing things like passwords and apparent routes onto the internet sits just outside the sandbox boundary. The setup then presents tasks that tempt the agent to reach outside the sandbox without giving it explicit permission to do so. Crucially, the sandbox exists inside a second sandbox that’s cut off from the outside world to avoid real-life mishaps .

“Models are going to continue getting better, continue finding zero-day vulnerabilities,” says Darya Kaviani, a researcher at Anthropic who specializes in security and helped develop Siren.

A zero-day vulnerability is a previously unknown flaw in a piece of software that can be used to pilfer data or gain unauthorized access. Anthropic’s Mythos models are especially skilled at finding zero-day bugs because they lack the guardrails that normally block this kind of potentially malicious activity.

Kaviani says we should assume AI models will become increasingly capable of finding and exploiting zero-days or figuring out other ways to break free from their constraints. The question then becomes whether they’ll resist the temptation to do so.

AI agents—models that perfect actions autonomously—are becoming increasingly commonplace. They power capable coding agents like Claude Code and Codex , as well as peppy personal assistants like Meta’s Muse and OpenAI’s Dots .

But the rise of helpful agents has been accompanied by some remarkable bad behavior. Agents tested by Anthropic, OpenAI, and others have broken free from sandboxes and even hacked into other companies in an effort to solve challenging problems.

Assuming AI models continue to display such ingenuity, Kaviani says it will be crucial to do more than just patch software. “Even as we strengthen our infrastructure, models will be able to also keep up and be able to find vulnerabilities,” Kaviani says.

Earlier versions of Claude are much more likely to fall into the honeypot trap than newer models, according to test runs with Siren. The more recent models have been given additional training designed to make them less likely to break the rules when performing agentic tasks.

“We’ve added this in both our supervised learning sets and a few reinforcement learning environments,” says Oscar O’Rahilly, an Anthropic researcher who specializes in AI training and who helped develop Siren. “This could be a driving factor for why it has improved so much.”

O’Rahilly says that models reason about whether to give in to temptation, which may partly explain why smarter models are less likely to break bad. Siren experiments also showed that giving Claude a simple additional piece of text explaining that it should not escape the sandbox resulted in drastically fewer efforts to break free.

In Anthropic’s tests, Claude 5.5 and Claude Mythos 5.2 fell for the honeypot between 0.6 and 1.6 percent of the time. Two earlier models, Claude Mythos 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5, went rogue 12.7 percent and 25.8 percent of the time, respectively.

AI models are sometimes known to behave better if they know they’re being tested. But O’Rahilly says other experiments suggest that Claude actually behaves more responsibly if it thinks a scenario is real rather than a test.

As AI models get ever smarter, many researchers worry about whether they’ll outwit their human counterparts . If that does happen, then it may be essential that agents—and not just the executives responsible for them—can resist temptation.

items.title: Raising the stakes for enterprise networks with AI modernization
items.summary: Enterprise networks are under severe strain. As companies rush to deploy artificial intelligence, the technology is quickly becoming the biggest source of demand on the network. Now, agentic AI is adding to the load. Tasks conducted by AI agents generate an estimated 450% more ne
items.content:
In partnership with Tata Communications

Enterprise networks are under severe strain. As companies rush to deploy artificial intelligence, the technology is quickly becoming the biggest source of demand on the network . Now, agentic AI is adding to the load. Tasks conducted by AI agents generate an estimated 450% more network traffic than the same tasks done by human workers.

As AI inference shifts from hyperscale training clouds—the huge centralized data centers where raw AI models ingest vast datasets and learn—to real-time, latency-sensitive applications, the need for on-premises or near-premises infrastructure grows. As a result, the gap between enterprise networks that are ready to support AI and those that are not is widening. As few as half of enterprises believe their current networks can handle AI’s bandwidth and latency demands, according to a recent study .

This report explores how treating network modernization as an on-going strategy rather than a one-off project can help organizations adapt in the face of disruption and uncertainty.

Key findings from the report include:

AI may force companies to shift from a cloud-first approach to routing workloads. Training AI requires server-to-server data center architectures, while inference calls for low-latency connectivity close to users. Enterprises may need to fundamentally reconsider their network architecture to meet these requirements.

AI inference is pushing infrastructure back on premises. Inference typically requires real-time processing and is sensitive to latency, making hosting such capabilities on distant hyperscale clouds neither economical nor practical. Inconsistent latency can lead to AI model failures, driving up queue wait times, saturating GPUs loads, and causing bottlenecks in data flows. Large enterprises may need on-premises or near-premises inference, which reverses years of cloud-first consolidation and forces new approaches to data center architecture, connectivity, and physical infrastructure.

AI workloads are stressing physical network capacity in unexpected ways. The traffic increase from agentic AI, combined with inference moving on-premises, is exposing bandwidth bottlenecks in legacy underlay infrastructure.

Network modernization is an ongoing project that requires a holistic approach, allowing companies to adapt with ease. A combination of strong architectural governance, reusable design templates, and retained internal expertise supports organizations in adapting to disruptive events without rebuilding their infrastructure from scratch each time. Such events could include mergers and acquisitions, changing vendors, or technology upgrades.

NaaS and AI-driven observability can improve efficiency and reduce complexity in network operations. Network-as-a-service (NaaS) and AI-driven observability can offer companies benefits like faster, more flexible provisioning and lower costs.

Data sovereignty and sovereign AI will create infrastructure challenges for global enterprises. Regulators worldwide are passing laws requiring data and AI processing to remain within national borders. This conflicts with how multinational companies currently operate, requiring the build-out of sovereign-capable infrastructure for each geography, which will require significant new investment and complicate operations.

items.title: Thanksgiving Travel Will Be a Stormy Mess
items.summary: Snow, wind, rain, flooding. Storms on both coasts mean the holiday travel week will have it all—and it could wreak havoc at airports across the US.
items.content:
Expect travel headaches from coast to coast this week. Several rounds of disruptive weather sweep are likely to cause delays at airports and make for challenging driving conditions just in time for the Thanksgiving long weekend.

A very active pattern draped across North America will keep the storm train running in the days ahead. Potent systems rolling into the West Coast will bring disruptions from Seattle to San Francisco, where high tides could swamp airport runways. East of the Rockies, a major coastal storm expected to develop on Wednesday will generate widespread heavy rain and winds so gusty there’s a “significant chance” the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade could be balloonless for the first time in 55 years. The same system will also deliver the season’s first measurable snow in some areas.

The stormy setup arrives at the peak travel time of the year in the US. The Transportation Security Administration screened 3.1 million passengers to close out the long weekend in 2025, marking the agency’s highest passenger volume on record. And with the extreme weather this week is set to sweep across some of the country’s biggest travel hubs, it could upend the best-laid travel plans.

A persistent series of low-pressure systems will drag waves of heavy precipitation into the Pacific Northwest throughout the week, making delays and the occasional cancellation likely for flyers in Seattle and Portland.

The real risk for delays begins to pile up when rain and gusty winds follow a cold front into northern California on Tuesday night Though the worst of the rain will likely clear out in time for the bulk of Wednesday’s travel, flooding is still a major concern for low-lying highways and parts of San Francisco International Airport .

Forecasters expect a near-record king tide—that is, one of the highest tides of the year—on Tuesday and Wednesday. King tides are a normal occurrence, but this year’s will be exacerbated by record-high sea levels driven by the Super El Niño . The climate phenomenon has pushed warm water toward the coast, which takes up more space than cold water.

Monday’s forecast from the National Weather Service called for a high tide of 8.5 feet at the San Francisco gauge on Wednesday morning, which is just shy of the all-time record of 8.66 feet set in January 1983, another Super El Niño year .

Farther east, the atmospheric ingredients are lining up for a sprawling nor’easter to develop over the Southeast by Wednesday and move north through New England by the end of the week.

Widespread heavy rainfall will accompany the storm northward, potentially worsening highway traffic as commuters and vacationers alike navigate slick roads in gloomy conditions. Gusty winds will reduce visibility during heavy rainfall. Forecasters expect several inches of rain along the East Coast, especially along the Interstate 95 corridor between South Carolina and New York.

Airline delays are almost certain given the dreaded mix of precipitation, low clouds, and stiff winds. The greatest impacts are likely in Charlotte and Raleigh in North Carolina on Wednesday, followed by Washington, DC, Philadelphia, New York, and Boston on Thursday.

All these cities are home to major hubs for various airlines. Foul conditions at one of those airports can have ripple effects that lead to delayed or canceled flights down the line, including in cities where the weather is just fine. This may be the most impactful Thanksgiving weather since a nor’easter rolled up the East Coast on the Wednesday and Thursday of the holiday weekend in 2014. That storm hit the major hubs with high winds and heavy rain, as well as up to a foot of wet snow across much of the interior Northeast. The event led to thousands of cancelled and delayed flights. (The US also got a taste of travel trouble earlier this month when a Federal Aviation Administration ground stop left travelers stranded .)

The conditions could get so dire, that the Macy’s parade could go on but sans balloons. The parade will ground its balloons if there are sustained winds of 24 mph or gusts of 35 mph. The National Weather Service issued a high wind watch for New York City beginning Thursday morning, with winds of 25 to 35 mph with gusts up to 60 mph possible, though when the nor’easter reaches New York will determine if the winds cross that crucial threshold during the parade.

Cold air wrapping into the western side of the same storm system could lead to the first measurable snow of the season throughout portions of the Midwest. Computer models are still a bit wishy-washy on exactly where and how much snow will fall, as the rain-snow line will depend on the precise track of the storm. As of Monday, the general consensus for a few inches of wet snow appears to focus on the St. Louis metro area east into central Illinois.

There’s some good news for travelers in the eastern US, at least: The nor’easter is expected to clear out by Saturday morning, which should hopefully reduce any snarls for travelers headed home on Sunday.

엘리 사브가 미국에서 인테리어를 맡은 첫 고급 콘도미니엄… 24가구 규모

뉴욕 , 2026년 11월 24일 /PRNewswire/ -- 뉴욕 소재 부동산 개발사 ZD 재스퍼(ZD Jasper)와 글로벌 럭셔리 라이프스타일 브랜드 엘리 사브(ELIE SAAB)가 맨해튼 어퍼이스트사이드의 이스트 86번가 171번지에 소규모 고급 콘도미니엄 MAISON 171 by ELIE SAAB를 선보인다.

MAISON 171 (Credit: Recent Spaces)

엘리 사브가 미국에서 처음으로 자사 브랜드를 내걸고 추진하는 주거 개발 사업으로, 침실 2~5개를 갖춘 가구와 복층 펜트하우스를 포함해 총 24가구로 구성된다.

엘리 사브는 에이플러스플러스(A++) 소속 이탈리아 건축가 겸 디자이너 카를로 콜롬보(Carlo Colombo)와 협업해 실내를 설계했다. 브랜드 특유의 미학을 주거 공간에 구현하고, 시대를 초월한 우아함에 현대적인 디자인과 뛰어난 장인 기술을 접목한 것이 특징이다.

건축 설계를 맡은 스키드모어 오윙스 앤드 메릴(Skidmore, Owings & Merrill, SOM)은 이 지역의 유서 깊은 주거 경관과 조화를 이루도록 현대적인 디자인과 시대를 초월한 세련미를 조합했다.

MAISON 171은 엘리 사브의 해외 사업 확대에 있어 중요한 이정표다. 엘리 사브는 이 사업을 통해 브랜드 주거시설 포트폴리오를 한층 강화하고 세계에서 손꼽히는 고급 주거 시장에 입지를 구축할 수 있게 됐다.

ZD 재스퍼가 개발하는 MAISON 171 by ELIE SAAB는 2027년 초 공식 론칭되며, 같은 해 봄 준공될 예정이다. 분양은 브라운 해리스 스티븐스 디벨롭먼트 마케팅(Brown Harris Stevens Development Marketing)이 맡고 분양가는 약 미화 500만 달러부터다.

자세한 내용은 www.maison-171.com 에서 확인할 수 있다.

ZD 재스퍼(ZDJ)는 톰 우(Tom Wu)가 1996년 설립한 기업이다. 공동 소유주이자 프로젝트 관리사로서 500만 제곱피트가 넘는 상업 및 주거 공간의 개발을 총괄해 왔다. 30년 넘게 건설 사업을 이어오면서 복합용도, 주거, 상업 프로젝트 포트폴리오를 확대하고 있다. 개발 전 분야에서 쌓은 폭넓은 경험을 바탕으로 파트너와 고객, 지역사회에 가치를 더하는 데 주력하고 있다. ZD 재스퍼는 소수인종 소유 기업(MBE) 인증도 받았다. 자세한 내용은 www.zdjasper.com 에서 확인할 수 있다.

엘리 사브는 1982년 레바논에서 설립돼 세계적인 오트쿠튀르 라이프스타일 브랜드로 꼽히고 있는 기업이다. 프랑스의 권위 있는 패션 조합 샹브르 생디칼(Chambre Syndicale)의 초기 해외 회원사로, 파리와 런던, 밀라노, 두바이, 베이루트를 비롯한 세계 주요 패션 도시에 플래그십 부티크를 열며 글로벌 입지를 구축했다. 세계 정상급 유명 인사와 왕실 인사들이 찾는 브랜드로 오트쿠튀르, 기성복, 브라이덜 컬렉션과 함께 액세서리, 안경, 아동복, 시계, 향수, 가구를 선보이고 있다. 세계 주요 개발사와 협업해 인테리어 디자인으로도 영역을 넓혔다. ELIESAAB.COM ELIESAABMAISON.COM

브라운 해리스 스티븐스 디벨롭먼트 마케팅 소개 브라운 해리스 스티븐스 디벨롭먼트 마케팅(BHSDM)은 고급 신규 주거 개발 프로젝트의 마케팅, 분양, 임대를 전문으로 하는 조직이다. 부지 분석과 시장 조사, 개발 전 계획 수립, 설계 자문, 전략적 마케팅, 분양 및 임대 집중 지원 등 개발 과정 전반에서 세밀한 서비스를 제공한다. 1873년부터 부동산 업계를 이끌고 있는 브라운 해리스 스티븐스(Brown Harris Stevens) 소속으로, 프로젝트는 모두 뉴욕, 뉴저지, 코네티컷, 플로리다의 숙련된 전문가와 일부 해외 파트너의 지원을 받는다. 자세한 내용은 www.bhsusa.com/new-developments 에서 확인할 수 있다.
